name: ch16-3-catastrophic-forgetting-lr
callout_title: Fun Fact: Tiptoeing inside a marble bowl
alt: A cartoon model robot tiptoeing carefully inside a smooth bowl labelled pretraining minimum, while a second oversized robot taking giant strides bounces out of the bowl with books labelled prior skills falling out of its backpack
caption_html: Figure 16.3.4: SFT learning rates sit two orders of magnitude below pretraining for a reason. Every step large enough to leave the basin of attraction risks dumping the prior skills the model spent millions of dollars learning.
prompt: Warm cartoon in Kurzgesagt-meets-XKCD style, navy and amber palette, white background, 16:9 landscape. A wide smooth marble bowl labelled 'pretraining minimum'. On the left, a small friendly model robot tiptoes carefully across the inside of the bowl with a tiny step labelled '2e-5'. On the right, an oversized robot is mid-leap, bouncing out of the bowl with a giant step labelled '2e-3' while a backpack labelled 'prior skills' tips over and books labelled MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval tumble out. The horizon shows a faint dotted line returning to the bowl. Hand-drawn watercolor texture, gentle expressions, no other text.

name: ch15-7-back-translation-tour
callout_title: Fun Fact: The grand back-translation tour
alt: A cartoon sentence holding a tiny suitcase travels by airplane from English to French to German to Chinese and back, returning home as the same meaning but with a fresh new outfit of synonyms
caption_html: Figure 15.7.1: Back-translation is a paraphrase passport. The sentence visits a few foreign languages, picks up new vocabulary, and comes home with the same meaning in a different outfit. For datasets under 1,000 examples, this round-trip alone often adds 2-5 points of accuracy.
prompt: Warm cartoon in Kurzgesagt-meets-XKCD style, navy and amber palette, white background, 16:9 landscape. A friendly anthropomorphized speech bubble character holding a tiny suitcase, hopping onto a small cartoon airplane. A curved dotted travel route loops through four small national landmarks: an Eiffel Tower (FR), a Brandenburg Gate (DE), a pagoda (CN), and back to a stack of books (EN). The bubble character arrives home wearing a new beret and scarf, still labelled with the same heart-shaped 'meaning' icon but with a tag reading 'fresh synonyms'. Cheerful watercolor, gentle, no other text.

name: ch22-4-three-vendor-podium
callout_title: Fun Fact: Three frontiers, three podiums, one moving leaderboard
alt: Three cartoon VLM robots standing on slightly different podiums in front of a treadmill leaderboard. GPT-4o is doing arithmetic on a chalkboard, Gemini holds an enormous scroll of context, Claude wears glasses and a tiny clipboard with the word hedging on it
caption_html: Figure 22.4.2: Three frontier VLMs, three different specialties. GPT-4o does arithmetic on receipts, Gemini swallows million-token scrolls, Claude squints carefully at small print. Any 1-3 point gap on a public benchmark is smaller than the variance from your prompt wording.
prompt: Warm cartoon in Kurzgesagt-meets-XKCD style, navy and amber palette, white background, 16:9 landscape. Three friendly robot characters on a low three-tier podium. Left robot labelled GPT-4o stands at a chalkboard doing arithmetic on a receipt, plus signs and dollar amounts floating above. Center robot labelled Gemini holds an enormous rolled-up scroll under one arm labelled '1M tokens' that trails off the side of the panel. Right robot labelled Claude wears tiny round glasses, holds a clipboard with a checkmark and the word 'hedge'. Behind them a leaderboard sign reads 'MMMU / MathVista / ChartQA' but the numbers are moving on a treadmill. Hand-drawn watercolor, gentle expressions, no other text.

name: ch23-3-zero123-imagination
callout_title: Fun Fact: Stable Diffusion already half-knew the back of the chair
alt: A cartoon Stable Diffusion character holds the front view of a wooden chair in one hand and, with a tiny mental lightbulb, imagines the back of the chair which materialises in a thought bubble. A label reads camera delta plus 90 degrees azimuth
caption_html: Figure 23.3.2: Zero-1-to-3 does not teach Stable Diffusion what chairs look like from behind. It just gives the model a tiny camera-pose ear-trumpet so it can finally answer the question it already knew the answer to.
prompt: Warm cartoon in Kurzgesagt-meets-XKCD style, navy and amber palette, white background, 16:9 landscape. A friendly cartoon diffusion-model character labelled 'Stable Diffusion' (a soft cloud-shaped robot) holds the front view of a small wooden chair in its left hand. From its head a thought-bubble emerges containing the back view of the same chair, which is materialising in dotted lines as it solidifies. A small dial on the cloud-robot's chest reads 'azimuth +90, elevation +10'. A tiny camera icon points along an orbit arc from front to back. Cheerful hand-drawn watercolor, gentle expression, no other text.

name: ch21-2-2d-position-map
callout_title: Fun Fact: Reading order vs the actual page
alt: Split panel cartoon. Left panel shows a BERT robot reading a form left-to-right top-to-bottom, dragging a tangled red string between the word Date and the answer 07-14-2024 that is 50 tokens away. Right panel shows a LayoutLM robot using an X-Y treasure-map ruler to find them only millimetres apart on the page
caption_html: Figure 21.2.2: A pure-text BERT has to walk a long reading-order path between 'Date:' and its answer. LayoutLM gets to use the page's actual geometry. That single 2D position embedding adds 13 F1 points on FUNSD.
prompt: Warm cartoon in Kurzgesagt-meets-XKCD style, navy and amber palette, white background, 16:9 landscape. Split panel cartoon. Left panel labelled 'BERT': a friendly robot reads a paper form left-to-right top-to-bottom, dragging a long tangled red string from the word 'Date:' all the way through 50 tokens of unrelated text to the answer '07/14/2024'. The robot looks tired. Right panel labelled 'LayoutLM': the same form, but a different robot holds a small X-Y ruler treasure-map and a glowing dotted line connects 'Date:' directly to '07/14/2024' a few millimetres away. Both robots are gentle and cheerful. Hand-drawn watercolor, no other text.

name: ch26-5-eight-component-cathedral
callout_title: Fun Fact: An agent is a tiny cathedral, not a chatbot
alt: A cartoon cross-section of a small cathedral. Eight friendly robot workers tend distinct rooms labelled Planner, Tool Router, Memory Manager, Execution Sandbox, Evaluator, Recovery Handler, Permissions Gate, Cost Controller. A small chatbot avatar peeks out only at the front door
caption_html: Figure 26.5.7: A production agent is a tiny cathedral with eight rooms. The model in the loop is the friendly receptionist at the door. The reliability lives in the other seven rooms, where the unhandled edge cases would otherwise be.
after_text: 26.5.1 The Eight Components of a Production Agent
prompt: Warm cartoon in Kurzgesagt-meets-XKCD style, navy and amber palette, white background, 16:9 landscape. A friendly cartoon cross-section of a small two-storey cathedral or dollhouse, with eight clearly separated rooms each tended by a tiny robot worker. Rooms are labelled in small banners: Planner, Tool Router, Memory Manager, Execution Sandbox, Evaluator, Recovery Handler, Permissions Gate, Cost Controller. A small chatbot avatar with a speech bubble peeks out only from the front door of the cathedral, looking innocent. Gentle hand-drawn watercolor, cosy lighting, no other text.

name: ch28-3-graduated-conveyor
callout_title: Fun Fact: Three lanes, one conveyor
alt: Three cartoon conveyor belts feeding into one human reviewer with green and red buttons. A green low-risk lane auto-passes a stack of summaries, a yellow medium-risk lane logs an outgoing email, and a red high-risk lane stops at the reviewer with a delete-records crate flashing
caption_html: Figure 28.3.3: Graduated autonomy in one conveyor belt. The agent is allowed to ship low-risk parcels without asking, medium-risk parcels after logging them, and never the red-flagged crates without a human signature.
prompt: Warm cartoon in Kurzgesagt-meets-XKCD style, navy and amber palette, white background, 16:9 landscape. A three-lane conveyor belt diagram. Top lane is green and labelled 'low risk: read, search, summarize' with little stacks of paper documents flowing past a smiling robot that waves them through. Middle lane is amber and labelled 'medium risk: send email, update record' with envelopes that pass through a small stamp labelled 'logged'. Bottom lane is red and labelled 'high risk: delete, purchase, modify access', with a crate flashing red sitting stopped at a human reviewer who holds a green APPROVE button in one hand and a red REJECT button in the other. Gentle hand-drawn watercolor, no other text.

name: ch27-4-toolbox-vs-swiss-army
callout_title: Fun Fact: Atomic tools beat a tangled Swiss-army knife
alt: Two cartoon agent robots side by side. Left robot wrestles with a giant Swiss-army knife labelled manage_database with 14 blades unfolded in confusing directions. Right robot calmly picks one of four neatly labelled hammers create_record, get_record, update_record, delete_record from a compartmented toolbox
caption_html: Figure 27.4.2: One multi-purpose tool gives the model a complicated interface to misuse. Four atomic tools each name themselves. The right-hand agent makes the same call in half the tokens, with half the retries.
prompt: Warm cartoon in Kurzgesagt-meets-XKCD style, navy and amber palette, white background, 16:9 landscape. Two cartoon agent robots side by side at a workbench. Left robot wrestles with an enormous tangled Swiss-army knife labelled 'manage_database(action=?)' that has fourteen blades unfolded in random directions, the robot looks frustrated and tokens are spilling out of its hands. Right robot calmly opens a clean wooden toolbox with four neatly compartmented little hammers labelled in small banners: create_record, get_record, update_record, delete_record. The right robot smiles, picks one hammer with confidence. Gentle hand-drawn watercolor, no other text.

name: ch33-2-three-cuts-buffet
callout_title: Fun Fact: Three RAG buffet stations, one VLM diner
alt: A cartoon buffet with three labelled stations: Image-as-Context with a small camera, Document-with-Images with a stack of PDFs, and Audio-Video RAG with a tiny film reel. A friendly VLM diner robot walks past sampling one plate from each, holding all three on a single tray
caption_html: Figure 33.2.3: Multimodal RAG is one umbrella term sheltering three different buffet stations. The VLM diner can sample from any of them, but each station has its own chunking, embedding, and prompt-engineering rules.
after_text: 33.2.1 The Three Cuts of Multimodal RAG
prompt: Warm cartoon in Kurzgesagt-meets-XKCD style, navy and amber palette, white background, 16:9 landscape. A friendly cartoon buffet counter with three clearly separated stations, each with a small overhead banner. Station 1 labelled 'Image-as-Context' shows a tray of cartoon photographs with a small camera icon. Station 2 labelled 'Document-with-Images' shows a stack of PDFs with little embedded charts. Station 3 labelled 'Audio / Video RAG' shows a tiny film reel and a small waveform on a plate. A friendly VLM diner robot walks past with one tray that has already accepted one plate from each station, looking happy. Hand-drawn watercolor, soft lighting, no other text.

name: ch36-2-library-vs-framework
callout_title: Fun Fact: Six function calls hiding under six abstractions
alt: Split panel cartoon. Left panel: a small thin library labelled six function calls is six neat building blocks the robot understands. Right panel: a thick framework labelled six abstractions is a tower of opaque crates with the same six blocks barely visible inside, while the robot scratches its head at three a m
caption_html: Figure 36.2.1: A thin library is six function calls you can read. A thick framework is six abstractions hiding the same six function calls. Choose the one you can debug at 3 a.m.
prompt: Warm cartoon in Kurzgesagt-meets-XKCD style, navy and amber palette, white background, 16:9 landscape. Split panel cartoon. Left panel labelled 'thin library': a small friendly robot calmly stacks six clearly labelled wooden blocks named encode, search, rerank, parse, chunk, hybrid in plain daylight. A small alarm clock above reads 3 AM and the robot is smiling, confident. Right panel labelled 'thick framework': the same six blocks are now hidden inside a teetering tower of opaque crates labelled 'Pipeline', 'Module', 'Signature', 'BaseRetriever', and the robot is frowning, holding a flashlight at 3 AM trying to peek inside. Gentle hand-drawn watercolor, no other text.

name: ch40-4-latency-budget-stopwatch
callout_title: Fun Fact: Every audio token costs 20 milliseconds of someone's life
alt: A cartoon stopwatch with a 300 ms target, an arrow pointing to a stacked latency bar made of segments labelled VAD, network, prompt, first token, codec, jitter buffer. A small budget jar holds tiny coins each labelled 20 ms
caption_html: Figure 40.4.3: A 300 ms TTFAT budget is a jar of about fifteen 20-millisecond coins. Each stage of the audio pipeline spends a few; the engineer's job is to keep enough in the jar that the user does not notice the wait.
prompt: Warm cartoon in Kurzgesagt-meets-XKCD style, navy and amber palette, white background, 16:9 landscape. A friendly cartoon stopwatch in the centre, its dial showing a target of 300 ms. To its right, a horizontal stacked bar chart of six segments labelled in tiny banners: VAD, network in, prompt processing, first token, codec decode, jitter buffer. Each segment is a different colour. On the left, a tiny glass jar labelled 'TTFAT budget' holds about fifteen small coins each stamped '20 ms'. A friendly engineer robot is pouring coins from the jar into the stacked bar, watching the stopwatch nervously. Hand-drawn watercolor, gentle, no other text.

name: ch44-5-five-drift-thermostats
callout_title: Fun Fact: One alarm for five very different fires
alt: A cartoon control room with five separate thermostats labelled Input, Model, Context, Performance, Cost, each ringing a different colour bell. A single tired engineer holds a fire extinguisher labelled tune the prompt and looks at all five
caption_html: Figure 44.5.2: Calling all five drifts 'quality dropped' is the most common post-launch mistake. Each thermostat needs its own dashboard, its own alarm, and its own response. The 'tune the prompt' extinguisher only fits one of them.
prompt: Warm cartoon in Kurzgesagt-meets-XKCD style, navy and amber palette, white background, 16:9 landscape. A cartoon production control room. Five different thermostats are mounted in a row on the back wall, each clearly labelled in a small banner: 'Input drift', 'Model drift', 'Context drift', 'Performance drift', 'Cost drift'. Each thermostat is ringing a slightly different coloured bell and showing a small icon (a crowd, a model weight, a stale calendar, a slow clock, a dollar sign). A single tired-looking engineer robot in pyjamas stands in front of them holding only one fire extinguisher labelled 'tune the prompt', looking overwhelmed but kind. Hand-drawn watercolor, soft warm lighting, no other text.
